reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premise that Co removal increases SFE; E4 discusses SFE in CoCrNi, not FeNiCrMn, and E1/E3 describe general behavior of CoCrFeMnNi without SFE comparisons. The link between SFE and dynamic behavior is not established by the cited passages, leaving the core mechanistic claims unsupported.
premises: Removing Co from CoCrFeMnNi increases the stacking fault energy (SFE) of the resulting FeNiCrMn alloy.
Higher SFE suppresses deformation twinning and promotes dislocation glide in this alloy system.
Under dynamic loading, higher SFE leads to higher strain-rate sensitivity and altered work-hardening (higher yield strength, less serration).
The baseline CoCrFeMnNi alloy exhibits deformation twinning and serrated flow under dynamic loading.
